rules.description: Every if statement must use a braced block for its consequent, with the body statements on separate lines from the condition. Fail both an unbraced body such as if (ready) return value; (even when the return is on the next line) and a one-line braced body such as if (ready) { return value; }. This applies to every if, including an else-if. A braced block with its body on following lines passes. Do not apply this rule to conditional expressions, comments, or strings containing example code.

A function must not expose a return value or success payload that is a union of a useful value and undefined, such as fn(...): Value | undefined. Wrappers do not make this acceptable: follow the returned payload through Promise, Result, jarl.Result, Option and other containers, at any nesting depth. Reject Result<Value | undefined, Error> and Promise<Result<Value | undefined, Error>> as well as Promise<Value | undefined>. This applies to function type aliases, call signatures, methods, and function-valued properties too. Fail an explicit union, a same-file alias that clearly resolves to that union, or an inferred return that visibly mixes a value with undefined or a fallthrough path, including a success payload passed to jarl.ok. void functions and undefined-only return values or success payloads pass because they are not Value | undefined unions. Optional parameters and optional fields within an otherwise defined returned object pass; a success payload of Value | undefined does not. Do not guess about unresolved types or external callees; require evidence in the supplied code.

Pass an existing services object directly to a function that needs services. Fail when code destructures or copies its service members merely to reconstruct a services object for another call, including a spread used only to narrow the object. Narrow the callee's parameter type instead. Reading a service to use it is fine. Creating the initial services object, adding a newly constructed service, replacing a service intentionally in a test, and building a separate options or request object are fine. Require visible evidence of reconstruction; do not guess about external callees.

Tests must assert behavior owned by the unit: returned data, search results, state changes, error handling, logged failures, or actions a control performs. Fail assertions that only pin fonts, sizes, colors, spacing, CSS, icons, layout position, static configuration, or behavior supplied entirely by a third-party library. Testing this project's own formatting or rendering function's output, a business sort order, and a boundary's response or failure message is valid. Test helpers with no assertions pass. Judge only assertions visible in this unit; do not infer missing tests or demand more happy-path tests.

Tests must use fakes for external HTTP, process IO, and clocks. Fail a test that visibly makes a real external HTTP request, starts a real external process, or waits for real time to pass to drive the behavior under test. In-process HTTP through a fake transport or Hono request/testClient is fine. Promise or event-loop synchronization without an elapsed-time delay is fine. The database exception is a test-owned Postgres started and stopped through @oligarchy/fake-postgres; that package's implementation and its own lifecycle tests may spawn Postgres. Require visible evidence of real external IO; do not assume a helper is live because its implementation is absent.
